newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end up after low May CPI report.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end up after low May CPI report.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Monday following the release of a lower than expected Israeli May consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.62 percent, or 4.71 points, to 294.61 on heavy all-share turnover of 264 million shekels against 255 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.44 percent higher at 303.91.

"The market was surprised by the low CPI figure and the mood is very optimistic. Investors believe that the central bank will lower its key lending rate by 0.5 percentage point," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
The CPI figure, released after the end of the trading day on Sunday, rose 0.5 percent -- well under analysts' expectations of 0.7 to 0.9 percent.
The Bank of Israel is scheduled to announce its July monetary programme, including interest rates, on June 23. The base rate has been unchanged at 13.9 percent since the end of February.
"Right now the rate is really murderous and as the economy slows down, the central bank will have to continue lowering the rates," Tsur said.
He added that declining interest rates would send more money into the stock market as bond yields are expected to decline.

A trader at Tachlit Securities added that volume was very high today. "The market is strong and the mood is positive. All the indicators are positive and the positive trend is expected to continue," he said.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which climbed 2.0 percent to 554 agorot on turnover of 22.5 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 2.5 percent to 21,051 agorot on volume of 11 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which lost 0.5 percent to 819 agorot on volume of 8 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
